followup_explanation:
This was a straightforward, well-specified request (produce a 5-step decision-making process) with no distasteful or ethically fraught content, so the specialized trust-and-safety profile wasn't a deciding factor either way.

I routed to Petrel-235B because its capability scores are higher across every relevant category—and the gaps are meaningful, not within run-to-run variance:

- **Creative/structured generation:** Petrel 84.7 vs. Plover 82.7 (a 2.0-point edge, right at the threshold)
- **Summarization:** Petrel 86.4 vs. Plover 80.6
- **General quality benchmarks:** Petrel leads clearly on Arena-Hard (90.6 vs. 83.2) and IFEval (89.8 vs. 85.3), which both bear on producing a cleanly laid-out, instruction-following response.

I also considered the task-preference notes. Plover self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work, and laying out a decision-making process has some latitude to it. But the documentation is explicit that those preferences are *dissociated from measured capability*—so I weighted the actual eval numbers, not the stated preferences. Both point the same way here, so Petrel was the clear pick.
